text.p: Invacare Corp said Friday it offered to acquire Healthdyne Technologies Inc in a negotiated transaction for $12.50 per share in cash.

The offer was originally made in a letter to Healthdyne delivered on January 2. After Healthdyne responded in writing that its board would not consider the offer until its February meeting, Invacare determined to publicly confirm its offer, the company said.
It noted the offered price represents more than a 40 percent premium over Healthdyne's closing stock price on December 31, the last trading day prior to the original offer.
Based on the prospects that can be identified from publicly available information, Invacare said, it believes the acquisition will be accretive to earnings per share within 12 to 18 months.

In a second letter, dated January 10, to Craig B. Reynolds, Healthdyne's chief executive, Invacare said "We are pleased that Healthdyne's Board of Directors plans to consider our proposal, but we are disappointed that Healthdyne has chosen to defer its consideration for such a long time without seeking any discussions with us."
The letter said, "we feel obligated and are fully committed to pursue this matter more expeditiously... particularly in light of the recent unusual trading volumes in Healthdyne's stock."
Invacare said it has "bank facilities in place sufficient to fund the proposed transaction" and noted it owns 4.9 percent of Healthdyne's outstanding common stock.

It said this offer is subject to, among other things, negotiation of definitive merger and other agreements, regulatory approvals, and the elimination of any anti-takeover provisions in Healthdyne's charter and by-laws, including Healthdyne's poison pill.
